L1: # Roam Alpha API
L2: 
L3: 【1†markdown version】 · 【2†view in Roam Research†roamresearch.com】
L4:   * Getting Started
L5:     * The Roam Alpha API is provided in the browser, letting you read and write data and drive the UI. It lives on the `window` object as `window.roamAlphaAPI` and is available from 【3†roam/js】/【4†roam/cljs】 code blocks, Roam Depot extensions, 【5†roam/render】, and the browser console.
L6:     * Despite the name, the API is no longer really "alpha" — we just can't change the name at this point. Breaking changes are rare and announced in the Change Log.
L7:     * For the ClojureScript version of this API, see the Reference section of 【4†roam/cljs】.
L8:     * Missing something? If the API doesn't have a function you think it should, reach out on Slack (【6†Contact Us】) — we're happy to make additions.
L9:   * Conventions
L10:     * Write promises resolve once Roam has applied the operation — after the triggering event and all of its descendant events are handled.
L11:       * The promise resolves before React re-renders, so if you manipulate the DOM right after a write you may still need a very small timeout.
L12:       * Failures reject the promise — use `.catch()`, or `try`/`catch` with `await`.
L13:     * Rate limit: rate-limited functions (all writes, plus a number of UI functions) share a budget of 1500 calls per 60 seconds; exceeding it throws.
L14:       * This is to protect your graph from runaway loops.
L15:       * If you are adding a lot of data at once, prefer creating from markdown.
L16:     * `q`, `pull`, `pull_many` and their variants time out after 20 seconds, throwing `Query and/or pull expression took too long to run.`
L17:     * uids
L18:       * Block and page uids are random 9-character strings — see `roamAlphaAPI.util.generateUID`.
L19:       * Daily note pages use the date as their uid, in `MM-DD-YYYY` format (e.g. `07-16-2026` for July 16th, 2026) — see `roamAlphaAPI.util.dateToPageUid`.
L20:       * uids can technically be any length and they don't have to be random, but some extensions might rely on it being 9 chars
L21:   * Reference
L22:     * `roamAlphaAPI.apiVersion` (string) — the API version, e.g. "1.1.3"; use it for feature detection
L23:     * `roamAlphaAPI.data`
L24:       * Description::
L25:         * Queries and reads, plus the write API for blocks, pages, and users.
L26:       * `roamAlphaAPI.data.q`
L27:         * Description::
L28:           * Query the graph with Datomic-flavored datalog. Synchronous.
L29:           * See the 【7†datomic docs†docs.datomic.com】 for the query syntax, 【8†learndatalogtoday.org†www.learndatalogtoday.org】 to learn it, and the 【9†datascript tests†github.com】 for good examples.
L30:           * The attributes you can query are documented on 【10†Data Model】.
L31:           * Legacy alias: `roamAlphaAPI.q` (older top-level name; prefer this namespaced path)
L32:           * Times out after 20 seconds by default; include a `:timeout <ms>` clause in the query to override.
L33:           * Datalog rules are supported — pass a rule set as an input bound to `%` in the `:in` clause; rules can be recursive.
L34:           * Function and predicate clauses are limited to DataScript's built-ins — comparisons, arithmetic, logic, collection helpers (`count`, `contains?`, `get`, ...), string helpers (`str`, `subs`, `clojure.string/includes?`/`starts-with?`/`ends-with?`/`blank?`), and regex (`re-find`, `re-matches`, `re-seq`, `re-pattern`). Custom functions can't be resolved from JS query strings.

L36:           * `query` (string, required) — the datalog query
L37:           * `...args` (optional) — additional inputs, bound to the query's `:in` clauses (the database itself is passed implicitly)

L39:           * Array of result tuples

L52:                         :in $ ?uid
L53:                         :where
L54:                         [?e :block/uid ?uid]
L55:                         [?e :block/string ?s]]`,
L56:                       "abc123xyz");

L58:       * `roamAlphaAPI.data.pull`
L59:         * Description::
L60:           * Declaratively fetch a (possibly nested) selection of attributes for one entity. Synchronous.
L61:           * See the 【11†datomic pull docs†docs.datomic.com】 — Roam uses 【12†datascript†github.com】 internally, which supports the majority of datomic syntax. In the JS API the pattern is a string rather than clojure data.

      'name: mg-verify-project-change\r\n' +
      'description: Verify an engineering change with project-appropriate tests, runtime behavior, and inspected evidence. Use before PR review or after review fixes, especially for RoamJS extensions and browser-facing Cybrarian or Discourse Graphs work. Do not invent visual proof for non-visual code.\r\n' +
      '---\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '# Verify Project Change\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Workflow reference\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Called before PR review and after review fixes by the full engineering/review workflows. Standalone verification remains supported.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      "Verify the ticket's `Done When` behavior, not merely that commands exit successfully.\r\n" +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Inputs\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '- Approved ticket or explicit acceptance criteria.\r\n' +
      '- Mode: `pre-pr` or `final`.\r\n' +
      '- Review target: working tree, branch, commit, or PR head.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Project routing\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Read [project routing](../mg-manage-codex-workflows/references/project-routing.md). Route by verified code ownership and changed runtime, not ticket ownership. DG `apps/roam` must select the DG Roam profile even though it runs inside Roam. Other DG apps must not load Roam browser helpers. Missing specialized sources block the affected verification rather than falling back to a generic profile.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Workflow\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '1. Read applicable `AGENTS.md` files and inspect the changed paths, repository scripts, and\r\n' +
      '   available project skills.\r\n' +
      '2. Resolve and record the exact target SHA. In `final` mode, confirm it matches the current PR\r\n' +
      '   head before testing and again before reporting success.\r\n' +
      '3. Read only the applicable profile in\r\n' +
      '   [references/project-profiles.md](references/project-profiles.md).\r\n' +
      "4. Run focused checks first, then the repository's proportionate full gate when available.\r\n" +
      '5. Before capture, resolve the output paths using [media storage and chat handoff](references/media-handoff.md): prefer the mounted Seagate drive for recordings and frame dumps, and honor stricter project rules. Exercise each user-visible acceptance criterion and relevant adjacent behavior in the real runtime. For Roam, read [exploratory verification](references/roam-exploration.md). Playwright or Agent Browser may explore interactively; durable UI tests are added for valuable regressions, not as a prerequisite to exploration. Capture meaningful screenshots/video; full Roam feature workflows require both in final mode unless waived.\r\n' +
      '6. Inspect every screenshot and the complete relevant video. Check page errors, console errors,\r\n' +
      '   failed requests, and final UI state; a render or recording alone is not acceptance.\r\n' +
      '7. Store receipts and screenshots under `local/scoped-workflow/<ticket-or-feature-key>/<sha>/` and keep them out of Git. Store video and frame dumps at the resolved media destination, which may be on the Seagate drive; record their absolute paths in the receipt.\r\n' +
      '8. Write `verification.json` containing mode, scope/acceptance criteria, optional ticket, source checkout, SHA, dirty-source fingerprint, loaded bundle hashes, graph/slot/session receipt, commands, behavioral checks, errors,\r\n' +
      '   artifacts with absolute paths and per-artifact inspection status, blockers, and overall status.\r\n' +
      '9. Deliver the saved video and final screenshots in the chat with previews and direct links,\r\n' +
      '   following the media handoff contract. Do this for complete, partial, and blocked reports;\r\n' +
      '   do not withhold saved media because inspection or another gate is pending.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Fail verification when the runtime cannot be exercised, required evidence cannot be inspected,\r\n' +
      'or the evidence belongs to another SHA. Distinguish change failures from unrelated baseline\r\n' +
      'failures. Report the smallest next action without expanding implementation scope.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Record behavioral status, evidence inspection status, and human acceptance separately. Final success requires the current PR SHA and a clean feature checkout (otherwise evidence describes uncommitted changes, not that PR). Preserve artifacts before fixture cleanup. Never claim a loader readiness probe alone proves the feature.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Evidence ledger\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Use the [evidence ledger contract](references/receipt.md) to render option A from `verification.json`. Keep required test/runtime gates, screenshot inspection, walkthrough inspection, tested SHA, blockers, next action, and human acceptance visible. Include baseline-error dispositions and per-artifact details in the saved evidence. Return the record to a calling workflow; show the ledger when verification owns the user handoff. The ledger never substitutes for saved media previews and direct links.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Human workflow guide and maintenance\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      "See [the workflow guide](../../workflows/index.html) and the linked RoamJS guide for invocation, phase ownership, and project adoption. After changing this workflow, update the owning YAML/guide source and run `npm run workflows:build`; for Roam-facing changes also run `node workflows/render.mjs` in RoamJS. Keep the human explanation aligned with the skill. See the guide's maintenance section for source ownership.\r\n"
  },

    value: '---\r\n' +
      'name: mg-review-pr-loop-full\r\n' +
      'description: "Run delegated review followed by the bounded PR comment loop for an approved engineering change. Use when explicitly invoked as the full-review shortcut; defaults to three PR comment rounds."\r\n' +
      '---\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '# Review PR Loop: Full Review\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Compose `$mg-delegated-full-review`, `$mg-verify-project-change`, and `$mg-review-pr-loop`.\r\n' +
      'Keep delegated review and PR comment monitoring in their separate skills; this shortcut owns\r\n' +
      'sequencing, in-scope fixes, and the transition to an open PR.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Inputs and entry\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Require an approved ticket URL or pasted scope boundary and the review target (existing PR,\r\n' +
      'branch, commit, or current changes). Preserve any supplied PR and base/head refs. Record the\r\n' +
      'current phase and head SHA so resumed work does not repeat completed phases or create another PR.\r\n' +
      'Load the three skills and their applicable references before executing their steps.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Sequence\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '1. Invoke `$mg-verify-project-change` in `pre-pr` mode, or reuse its successful receipt only when scope, source checkout, SHA, dirty-source fingerprint, bundle checksum, and required checks still match. Stop if verification fails.\r\n' +
      '2. Invoke `$mg-delegated-full-review` with the same target and approved scope. The selected\r\n' +
      '   reviewer owns the single read-only review subagent; do not create another dispatcher.\r\n' +
      '3. Classify findings as in-scope, out-of-scope, ambiguous, or safety-blocking. Fix in-scope\r\n' +
      '   findings in the primary context, reverify, and repeat delegated review for the updated target\r\n' +
      '   until no actionable in-scope findings remain, with a default ceiling of three fix/review cycles. Stop if a review fails, findings cannot be\r\n' +
      '   resolved, or a round makes no progress. Stop for user input on ambiguous or safety-blocking\r\n' +
      '   findings, and preserve out-of-scope findings for the final report.\r\n' +
      "4. Once delegated review is clean, create or update the PR within the user's authorization.\r\n" +
      '   Reuse an existing PR. If publication is not authorized, leave the change reviewable and ask\r\n' +
      '   before publishing; do not infer authorization from a read-only review request.\r\n' +
      '5. Invoke `$mg-review-pr-loop` with the open PR, approved scope, expected-reviewer overrides,\r\n' +
      '   and `max_rounds` (default `3`). That skill exclusively owns PR comment monitoring and its\r\n' +
      '   stopping rules. A timeout or unresolved finding is a partial result, not a clean review.\r\n' +
      '6. After a clean PR comment loop, invoke `$mg-verify-project-change` in `final` mode against\r\n' +
      '   the current PR head. Rebuild and reload after review changes. For user-visible Roam features, require inspected screenshots and a basic walkthrough video of the final feature unless the user explicitly waives media. Use the verifier’s Roam exploration reference. A recording failure leaves the media gate incomplete even if behavior passed.\r\n' +
      '7. If asked for manual testing, invoke the owning extension loader with “for me to test,” leave its fixture and headed browser alive, and provide the receipt and stop command.\r\n' +
      '8. Report the PR, SHA, delegated-review result, comment rounds, verification,\r\n' +
      '   and unresolved findings or blockers. Deliver the saved video and final screenshots in this chat\r\n' +
      "   as previews plus direct links using the verifier's\r\n" +
      '   [media storage and chat handoff](../mg-verify-project-change/references/media-handoff.md).\r\n' +
      '   Apply this to partial or blocked outcomes as well; label uninspected media clearly.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Stop at the first failed gate. Do not merge, release, close the ticket, or create follow-up\r\n' +
      'issues. This shortcut does not rerun ticket creation or implementation planning.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Gate ladder receipt\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      'Use the [gate ladder receipt](references/receipt.md) for handoffs. Show pre-PR verification, independent review, the PR comment loop, and final evidence with the exact target SHA and first unfinished gate. Keep local fix/review cycles separate from PR comment rounds; unknown counts stay unknown. Return child records to the parent when it owns the final receipt instead of repeating every visualization.\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      '## Human workflow guide and maintenance\r\n' +
      '\r\n' +
      "See [the workflow guide](../../workflows/index.html) and the linked RoamJS guide for invocation, phase ownership, and project adoption. After changing this workflow, update the owning YAML/guide source and run `npm run workflows:build`; for Roam-facing changes also run `node workflows/render.mjs` in RoamJS. Keep the human explanation aligned with the skill. See the guide's maintenance section for source ownership.\r\n"

# Vercel React Best Practices

Comprehensive performance optimization guide for React and Next.js applications, maintained by Vercel. Contains 64 rules across 8 categories, prioritized by impact to guide automated refactoring and code generation.

## When to Apply

Reference these guidelines when:

- Writing new React components or Next.js pages
- Implementing data fetching (client or server-side)
- Reviewing code for performance issues
- Refactoring existing React/Next.js code
- Optimizing bundle size or load times

## Rule Categories by Priority

| Priority | Category                  | Impact      | Prefix       |
| -------- | ------------------------- | ----------- | ------------ |
| 1        | Eliminating Waterfalls    | CRITICAL    | `async-`     |
| 2        | Bundle Size Optimization  | CRITICAL    | `bundle-`    |
| 3        | Server-Side Performance   | HIGH        | `server-`    |
| 4        | Client-Side Data Fetching | MEDIUM-HIGH | `client-`    |
| 5        | Re-render Optimization    | MEDIUM      | `rerender-`  |
| 6        | Rendering Performance     | MEDIUM      | `rendering-` |
| 7        | JavaScript Performance    | LOW-MEDIUM  | `js-`        |
| 8        | Advanced Patterns         | LOW         | `advanced-`  |

## Quick Reference

### 1. Eliminating Waterfalls (CRITICAL)

- `async-defer-await` - Move await into branches where actually used
- `async-parallel` - Use Promise.all() for independent operations
- `async-dependencies` - Use better-all for partial dependencies
- `async-api-routes` - Start promises early, await late in API routes
- `async-suspense-boundaries` - Use Suspense to stream content

### 2. Bundle Size Optimization (CRITICAL)

- `bundle-barrel-imports` - Import directly, avoid barrel files
- `bundle-dynamic-imports` - Use next/dynamic for heavy components
- `bundle-defer-third-party` - Load analytics/logging after hydration
- `bundle-conditional` - Load modules only when feature is activated
- `bundle-preload` - Preload on hover/focus for perceived speed

### 3. Server-Side Performance (HIGH)

- `server-auth-actions` - Authenticate server actions like API routes
- `server-cache-react` - Use React.cache() for per-request deduplication
- `server-cache-lru` - Use LRU cache for cross-request caching
- `server-dedup-props` - Avoid duplicate serialization in RSC props
- `server-hoist-static-io` - Hoist static I/O (fonts, logos) to module level
- `server-serialization` - Minimize data passed to client components
- `server-parallel-fetching` - Restructure components to parallelize fetches
- `server-after-nonblocking` - Use after() for non-blocking operations

### 4. Client-Side Data Fetching (MEDIUM-HIGH)

- `client-swr-dedup` - Use SWR for automatic request deduplication
- `client-event-listeners` - Deduplicate global event listeners
- `client-passive-event-listeners` - Use passive listeners for scroll
- `client-localstorage-schema` - Version and minimize localStorage data

### 5. Re-render Optimization (MEDIUM)

- `rerender-defer-reads` - Don't subscribe to state only used in callbacks
- `rerender-memo` - Extract expensive work into memoized components
- `rerender-memo-with-default-value` - Hoist default non-primitive props
- `rerender-dependencies` - Use primitive dependencies in effects
- `rerender-derived-state` - Subscribe to derived booleans, not raw values
- `rerender-derived-state-no-effect` - Derive state during render, not effects
- `rerender-functional-setstate` - Use functional setState for stable callbacks
- `rerender-lazy-state-init` - Pass function to useState for expensive values
- `rerender-simple-expression-in-memo` - Avoid memo for simple primitives
- `rerender-split-combined-hooks` - Split hooks with independent dependencies
- `rerender-move-effect-to-event` - Put interaction logic in event handlers
- `rerender-transitions` - Use startTransition for non-urgent updates
- `rerender-use-deferred-value` - Defer expensive renders to keep input responsive
- `rerender-use-ref-transient-values` - Use refs for transient frequent values
- `rerender-no-inline-components` - Don't define components inside components

### 6. Rendering Performance (MEDIUM)

- `rendering-animate-svg-wrapper` - Animate div wrapper, not SVG element
- `rendering-content-visibility` - Us---
name: scope-check
description: Compare a pull request or Git diff with a Linear engineering ticket's Done When criteria and produce a copy-ready PR scope check. Use when preparing or reviewing a PR, checking whether an implementation introduced broader abstractions or unsupported cases, or documenting why added scope is required now.
---

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.
# Project verification profiles

Select by the changed runtime, not only by repository name.

## RoamJS extension

- Identify the app from `apps/<slug>`; do not substitute `package.json.name` when it differs.
- Build with the app's current repository command. Do not edit generated output to satisfy the
  loader.
- Load both skills from the owning RoamJS central collection. Use `$roamjs-load-extension` to load the built folder and `$roamjs-playwright-session` for a
  logged-in real-Roam session.
- Follow [Roam exploratory verification](roam-exploration.md) for acceptance and nearby behavior.
- Agent Browser recording stops and saves while the page remains open. Native Playwright video finalizes after page/context close; keep its Video handle and await saveAs after closing. Inspect the saved file before calling media complete.

## Discourse Graphs Roam extension

- For DG `apps/roam`, load `$dg-roam-load-extension` and `$dg-roam-playwright-session` from the DG repository's `.agents/skills` directory.
- Follow their build, account-slot, profile, activation, and proof instructions. Do not substitute the RoamJS helpers based only on the Roam runtime.
- Use one session lifecycle: the loader composes with session selection; do not independently launch a second browser just because both skills were read.
- Apply the parent verifier's acceptance checks, inspected evidence, and target-SHA rules.

## Discourse Graphs website, Obsidian, or backend

- Read the affected app's `AGENTS.md`, scripts, and applicable repository skills.
- For the website, use the repository's test gate and a browser flow when the changed behavior is browser-facing.
- For Obsidian, backend, and libraries, use the matching runtime/fixture/integration profile below. Do not load either Roam browser helper pair.

## Browser-facing Cybrarian or other projects

- Identify the affected workspace and build its dependencies before isolated typechecks when the
  monorepo requires compiled package output.
- Run its unit/integration gate and a Playwright flow covering the ticket's user behavior.
- Capture visual evidence only for meaningful UI behavior; include server/browser errors and the
  final URL or route.

## macOS Next.js localhost recording preflight

Use this sequence when recording a Next.js runtime on a Mac:

1. Stop only the development or production server started for the current verification before
   rebuilding. Do not kill an unrelated process merely because it owns the preferred port.
2. Build workspace dependencies and the Next.js app to completion. For `next start`, confirm the
   expected `.next` server artifacts exist before launching it; do not rebuild while it is running.
3. Start the server in a long-lived process on an explicit port. Wait for Next.js to report
   `Ready`, confirm the target route responds successfully (for example with macOS `curl`), then
   poll the server once more to prove it is still alive.
4. Open a fresh browser tab for every recording attempt. Never reuse a tab that encountered a
   connection failure, internal browser error page, blocked navigation, or browser safety refusal.
5. Apply a viewport override, navigation, or reload in its own step. Immediately verify the exact
   localhost URL, page title, expected DOM, server output, and browser/page errors before clicking
   controls or starting capture.
6. Do not batch unverified setup with the interaction sequence. Begin recording only after the
   preflight is clean, and keep the same server process alive without rebuilding throughout capture.
7. If the server exits or the route stops responding, discard the tab and partial evidence. Repair
   or rebuild the app, restart the server, wait for `Ready`, repeat the route probe, and use a new tab.
8. Decode and inspect the complete video, not only sampled frames. Record the server command, route,
   errors, artifact path, and exact tested SHA in `verification.json`.

## Obsidian, library, backend, or CLI

- Use the repository's unit, integration, fixture, build, or runtime harness for the affected
  surface.
- Do not manufacture screenshots or video for non-visual behavior.
- If the only trustworthy verification is manual or requires an unavailable host application,
  report that limitation and do not mark the runtime gate complete.

## Unknown project

Inspect package scripts, CI configuration, existing tests, and repository instructions. Choose
the smallest test set that proves the acceptance criteria, then add broader regression coverage
in proportion to risk.

name: scope-check
description: Compare a pull request or Git diff with a Linear engineering ticket's Done When criteria and produce a copy-ready PR scope check. Use when preparing or reviewing a PR, checking whether an implementation introduced broader abstractions or unsupported cases, or documenting why added scope is required now.
---

# Scope Check

Compare the completed change with its acceptance boundary. Return a copy-ready `Scope check` section unless the user requests the analysis too.

## Gather the Inputs

1. Resolve the Linear issue from an explicit `ENG-###` identifier, then from the PR or branch name. Fetch the issue with the Linear connector. If it is unavailable, ask for the ticket's `Problem`, `Solution`, and `Done When` sections.
2. Treat `Done When` as the acceptance boundary. Use `Problem` and `Solution` only to clarify that boundary, not to silently expand it.
3. Resolve the final change set from the supplied diff or PR. For a PR, inspect its metadata and complete diff. For the current branch, compare it with the PR base branch and include staged and unstaged changes.
4. Read linked decisions or ticket comments only when they explain an apparent scope expansion.

## Evaluate Scope

Map every material behavior or architectural change to a `Done When` criterion.

- Treat implementation details, tests, documentation, and generated files required to satisfy `Done When` as in scope.
- Flag broader abstractions, unrelated refactors, new dependencies, migrations, or support for cases not required by `Done When`.
- Do not treat a change as in scope only because it is useful or adjacent.

For each scope expansion, determine:

1. What broader abstraction or additional case was introduced?
2. Which current use case or ticket requires it, and why must it be included now rather than deferred?
3. Was anyone affected or consulted, and where is the discussion or decision recorded?

Do not invent missing justification. Mark it `Not documented` and recommend recording it in a Linear comment before the PR is merged.

## Format the Result

Use this form when the diff stays within scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: None.
```

Use this form when the diff expands scope:

```markdown
## Scope check

- [x] Ran `$scope-check` against ENG-#### and the final diff.
- Scope beyond `Done When`: <what changed>
- Required now: <use case or ticket and why it cannot be deferred>
- Anyone affected or consulted: <Yes, No, or Not documented>
- Decision: <link to the discussion or decision, or `Not documented`>
```

If the ticket or diff cannot be resolved, leave the checkbox unchecked and state exactly what input is missing. Keep findings short and evidence-based.

Do not modify the issue, PR, or implementation unless the user explicitly asks.
# Project verification profiles

Select by the changed runtime, not only by repository name.

## RoamJS extension

- Identify the app from `apps/<slug>`; do not substitute `package.json.name` when it differs.
- Build with the app's current repository command. Do not edit generated output to satisfy the
  loader.
- Load both skills from the owning RoamJS central collection. Use `$roamjs-load-extension` to load the built folder and `$roamjs-playwright-session` for a
  logged-in real-Roam session.
- Follow [Roam exploratory verification](roam-exploration.md) for acceptance and nearby behavior.
- Agent Browser recording stops and saves while the page remains open. Native Playwright video finalizes after page/context close; keep its Video handle and await saveAs after closing. Inspect the saved file before calling media complete.

## Discourse Graphs Roam extension

- For DG `apps/roam`, load `$dg-roam-load-extension` and `$dg-roam-playwright-session` from the DG repository's `.agents/skills` directory.
- Follow their build, account-slot, profile, activation, and proof instructions. Do not substitute the RoamJS helpers based only on the Roam runtime.
- Use one session lifecycle: the loader composes with session selection; do not independently launch a second browser just because both skills were read.
- Apply the parent verifier's acceptance checks, inspected evidence, and target-SHA rules.

## Discourse Graphs website, Obsidian, or backend

- Read the affected app's `AGENTS.md`, scripts, and applicable repository skills.
- For the website, use the repository's test gate and a browser flow when the changed behavior is browser-facing.
- For Obsidian, backend, and libraries, use the matching runtime/fixture/integration profile below. Do not load either Roam browser helper pair.

## Browser-facing Cybrarian or other projects

- Identify the affected workspace and build its dependencies before isolated typechecks when the
  monorepo requires compiled package output.
- Run its unit/integration gate and a Playwright flow covering the ticket's user behavior.
- Capture visual evidence only for meaningful UI behavior; include server/browser errors and the
  final URL or route.

## macOS Next.js localhost recording preflight

Use this sequence when recording a Next.js runtime on a Mac:

1. Stop only the development or production server started for the current verification before
   rebuilding. Do not kill an unrelated process merely because it owns the preferred port.
2. Build workspace dependencies and the Next.js app to completion. For `next start`, confirm the
   expected `.next` server artifacts exist before launching it; do not rebuild while it is running.
3. Start the server in a long-lived process on an explicit port. Wait for Next.js to report
   `Ready`, confirm the target route responds successfully (for example with macOS `curl`), then
   poll the server once more to prove it is still alive.
4. Open a fresh browser tab for every recording attempt. Never reuse a tab that encountered a
   connection failure, internal browser error page, blocked navigation, or browser safety refusal.
5. Apply a viewport override, navigation, or reload in its own step. Immediately verify the exact
   localhost URL, page title, expected DOM, server output, and browser/page errors before clicking
   controls or starting capture.
6. Do not batch unverified setup with the interaction sequence. Begin recording only after the
   preflight is clean, and keep the same server process alive without rebuilding throughout capture.
7. If the server exits or the route stops responding, discard the tab and partial evidence. Repair
   or rebuild the app, restart the server, wait for `Ready`, repeat the route probe, and use a new tab.
8. Decode and inspect the complete video, not only sampled frames. Record the server command, route,
   errors, artifact path, and exact tested SHA in `verification.json`.

## Obsidian, library, backend, or CLI

- Use the repository's unit, integration, fixture, build, or runtime harness for the affected
  surface.
- Do not manufacture screenshots or video for non-visual behavior.
- If the only trustworthy verification is manual or requires an unavailable host application,
  report that limitation and do not mark the runtime gate complete.

## Unknown project

Inspect package scripts, CI configuration, existing tests, and repository instructions. Choose
the smallest test set that proves the acceptance criteria, then add broader regression coverage
in proportion to risk.

---
name: turborepo
description: |
  Turborepo monorepo build system guidance. Triggers on: turbo.json, task pipelines,
  dependsOn, caching, remote cache, the "turbo" CLI, --filter, --affected, CI optimization, environment
  variables, internal packages, monorepo structure/best practices, and boundaries.

  Use when user: configures tasks/workflows/pipelines, creates packages, sets up
  monorepo, shares code between apps, runs changed/affected packages, debugs cache,
  or has apps/packages directories.
metadata:
  version: 2.10.1-canary.1
---

# Turborepo Skill

Build system for JavaScript/TypeScript monorepos. Turborepo caches task outputs and runs tasks in parallel based on dependency graph.

## IMPORTANT: Package Tasks, Not Root Tasks

**Prefer package tasks over Root Tasks.**

When creating tasks/scripts/pipelines, you MUST default to package tasks:

1. Add the script to each relevant package's `package.json`
2. Register the task in root `turbo.json`
3. Root `package.json` only delegates via `turbo run <task>`

**DO NOT** put task logic in root `package.json` when it can live in packages. This defeats Turborepo's parallelization.

```json
// DO THIS: Scripts in each package
// apps/web/package.json
{ "scripts": { "build": "next build", "lint": "eslint .", "test": "vitest" } }

// apps/api/package.json
{ "scripts": { "build": "tsc", "lint": "eslint .", "test": "vitest" } }

// packages/ui/package.json
{ "scripts": { "build": "tsc", "lint": "eslint .", "test": "vitest" } }
```

```json
// turbo.json - register tasks
{
  "tasks": {
    "build": { "dependsOn": ["^build"], "outputs": ["dist/**"] },
    "lint": {},
    "test": { "dependsOn": ["build"] }
  }
}
```

```json
// Root package.json - ONLY delegates, no task logic
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "turbo run build",
    "lint": "turbo run lint",
    "test": "turbo run test"
  }
}
```

```json
// DO NOT DO THIS - defeats parallelization
// Root package.json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "cd apps/web && next build && cd ../api && tsc",
    "lint": "eslint apps/ packages/",
    "test": "vitest"
  }
}
```

Root Tasks (`//#taskname`) are ONLY for tasks that truly cannot exist in packages, such as Vitest Projects' `//#test`, repo-wide release scripts, or tooling that does not invoke `turbo` itself.

## Secondary Rule: `turbo run` vs `turbo`

**Always use `turbo run` when the command is written into code:**

```json
// package.json - ALWAYS "turbo run"
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "turbo run build"
  }
}
```

```yaml
# CI workflows - ALWAYS "turbo run"
- run: turbo run build --affected
```

**The shorthand `turbo <tasks>` is ONLY for one-off terminal commands** typed directly by humans or agents. Never write `turbo build` into package.json, CI, or scripts.

## Quick Decision Trees

### "I need to configure a task"

```
Configure a task?
├─ Define task dependencies → references/configuration/tasks.md
├─ Lint/check-types (parallel + caching) → Use Transit Nodes pattern (see below)
├─ Specify build outputs → references/configuration/tasks.md#outputs
├─ Handle environment variables → references/environment/RULE.md
├─ Set up dev/watch tasks → references/configuration/tasks.md#persistent
├─ Package-specific config → references/configuration/RULE.md#package-configurations
└─ Global settings (cacheDir, daemon) → references/configuration/global-options.md
```

### "My cache isn't working"

```
Cache problems?
├─ Tasks run but outputs not restored → Missing `outputs` key
├─ Cache misses unexpectedly → references/caching/gotchas.md
├─ Need to debug hash inputs → Use --summarize or --dry
├─ Want to skip cache entirely → Use --force or cache: false
├─ Remote cache not working → references/caching/remote-cache.md
└─ Environment causing misses → references/environment/gotchas.md
```

### "I want to run only changed packages"

```
Run only what changed?
├─ Changed packages + dependents (RECOMMENDED) → turbo run build --affected
├─ Custom base branch → --affected --affected-base=origin/develop
├─ Manual git comparison → --filter=...[origin/main]
└─ See all filter options → references/filtering/RULE.md
```

**`--affected` is the primary way to run only changed packages.** It automatically compares against the default branch and includes dependents.

### "I want to filter packages"

```
Filter packages?
├─ Only changed packages → --affected (see above)
├─ By package name → --filter=web
├─ By directory → --filter=./apps/*
├─ Package + dependencies → --filter=web...
├─ Package + dependents → --filter=...web
└─ Complex combinations → references/filtering/patterns.md
```

### "Environment variables aren't working"

```
Environment issues?
├─ Vars not available at runtime → Strict mode filtering (default)
├─ Cache hits with wrong env → Var not in `env` key
├─ .env changes not causing rebuilds → .env not in `inputs`
├─ CI variables missing → references/environment/gotchas.md
└─ Framework vars (NEXT_PUBLIC_*) → Auto-included via inference
```

### "I need to set up CI"

```
CI setup?
├─ GitHub Actions → references/ci/g---
name: dg-roam-load-extension
description: Build, register, activate, and verify the local Discourse Graphs Roam extension, then run an optional feature test in the same Playwright context. Use for live apps/roam proof on Windows or macOS without repeating browser, login, and folder-loading setup.
---

# DG Roam Load Extension

Use this skill for one complete lifecycle: build `apps/roam`, open an authenticated slot, register `apps/roam/dist`, activate it, verify DG runtime readiness, run an optional caller test, capture proof, and close.

It composes with `dg-roam-playwright-session` for account/profile selection.

## Quick Start

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1
```

Use another slot for isolated work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 2
```

The script builds by default, verifies `window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder`, checks the DG settings UI, and writes proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

To add feature-specific assertions without copying the loader, pass an ESM test module:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1 --test-module ./local/roam-playwright/feature-proof.mjs
```

```js
export default {
  readySelector: "[data-testid='feature-ready']",
  async ready({ page }) {
    return page.evaluate(() => Boolean(window.myFeature?.ready));
  },
  async run({ page, outDir }) {
    await page.getByText("Expected output").waitFor();
    return { assertion: "passed" };
  },
  async cleanup({ page, state }) {
    // Remove only fixtures created by run().
  },
};
```

`run()` starts only after the standard DG runtime proof and any caller readiness hook succeeds. `cleanup()` runs when `run()` started, including after a failed assertion. Return JSON-serializable proof values.

## Options

- `--slot 1|2|3`: Select the Roam account/profile.
- `--skip-build`: Load the existing `apps/roam/dist` without rebuilding.
- `--headed`: Run with a visible Chromium window.
- `--keep-open`: Leave the browser open after loading.
- `--dist <path>`: Load a different Roam extension folder. Use only when intentionally testing another build output.
- `--registration-name <name>`: Developer Extensions row name. Defaults to the built folder name, usually `dist`.
- `--test-module <path>`: Caller readiness, test, and cleanup hooks. Absolute Windows paths and paths containing spaces are supported.
- `--out <path>` and `--screenshot-name <name>`: Proof artifact locations.
- `--timeout <ms>`: UI and readiness timeout. Defaults to `45000`.

## Folder Loading

Roam Depot's folder button calls `window.showDirectoryPicker()`, not an `<input type="file">`. The script installs a temporary in-page directory-picker shim backed by the files in `apps/roam/dist`.

The loader uses native Playwright clicks for developer mode and folder controls. It treats the extension row as registration only, then clicks the header or row refresh control when present and waits for DG runtime proof. Roam versions that activate automatically may expose no refresh control.

An IndexedDB clone warning for the fake directory handle is expected and classified separately. Other page exceptions fail the run. `last-run.json` includes phase timings and bounded browser diagnostics; failures also capture a dedicated screenshot and compact DOM state.

## Safety Notes

- Do not commit `.env`, browser profiles, or artifacts.
- Do not commit real Roam test account emails, graph names, graph URLs, or proof screenshots.
- Keep feature fixtures, command interactions, and assertions in the caller module. Do not add them to the generic loader.
- Do not change Supabase local/branch/production config as part of this skill.
- Do not run production-backend smoke tests in this workflow.
---
name: dg-roam-playwright-session
description: Open one authenticated Roam Research Playwright context with a Discourse Graphs test slot on Windows or macOS. Use when testing apps/roam, capturing proof, inspecting live Roam behavior, or reusing the same page and profile across several checks.
---

# DG Roam Playwright Session

Use this skill to open a real Roam Research graph once, run all checks in the returned context, capture proof, and close it cleanly.

Secrets must live only in the ignored `apps/roam/.env`. Do not print, inspect, or commit passwords, cookies, local storage, or Playwright profile contents.

## Quick Start

Open slot 1:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 1
```

Use slots 2 or 3 for isolated concurrent work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 2
pnpm --filter roam playwright:open -- --slot 3
```

The script writes screenshots and JSON proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

For loading `apps/roam/dist` and running a feature test in the same context, use `dg-roam-load-extension` instead of creating a temporary browser harness.

## Environment

The ignored `apps/roam/.env` should contain one set per slot:

```sh
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_EMAIL_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PASSWORD_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_GRAPH_URL_1=
DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_1=
```

Repeat for `_2` and `_3`.

Account emails and graph URLs are intentionally required from the ignored app `.env`. Do not add real test account identifiers, graph names, graph URLs, or passwords to committed files.

Profile directories default to ignored local paths under `local/roam-playwright/profiles/`.

The repo-relative `.env`, profile, and artifact paths work on Windows and macOS. Override them only when the slot needs a different local location:

- `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_ENV_PATH`: alternate ignored environment file.
- `DG_ROAM_PLAYWRIGHT_PROFILE_DIR_<slot>` or `--profile-dir`: slot profile.
- `--out`: proof output directory.

When importing `openRoamSession`, keep the returned session and call `session.close()` in `finally`. A failed navigation or readiness check closes the context automatically.

## Safety Notes

- Only one Chromium process can own a persistent profile at a time.
- A profile-lock error identifies the occupied slot and path. Close that session or use another `--slot`; do not delete lock files.
- Use `--headed --allow-login` if manual login recovery is needed.
- Credential values never belong in result JSON or diagnostics.

name: turborepo
description: |
  Turborepo monorepo build system guidance. Triggers on: turbo.json, task pipelines,
  dependsOn, caching, remote cache, the "turbo" CLI, --filter, --affected, CI optimization, environment
  variables, internal packages, monorepo structure/best practices, and boundaries.

  Use when user: configures tasks/workflows/pipelines, creates packages, sets up
  monorepo, shares code between apps, runs changed/affected packages, debugs cache,
  or has apps/packages directories.
metadata:
  version: 2.10.1-canary.1
---

# Turborepo Skill

Build system for JavaScript/TypeScript monorepos. Turborepo caches task outputs and runs tasks in parallel based on dependency graph.

## IMPORTANT: Package Tasks, Not Root Tasks

**Prefer package tasks over Root Tasks.**

When creating tasks/scripts/pipelines, you MUST default to package tasks:

1. Add the script to each relevant package's `package.json`
2. Register the task in root `turbo.json`
3. Root `package.json` only delegates via `turbo run <task>`

**DO NOT** put task logic in root `package.json` when it can live in packages. This defeats Turborepo's parallelization.

```json
// DO THIS: Scripts in each package
// apps/web/package.json
{ "scripts": { "build": "next build", "lint": "eslint .", "test": "vitest" } }

// apps/api/package.json
{ "scripts": { "build": "tsc", "lint": "eslint .", "test": "vitest" } }

// packages/ui/package.json
{ "scripts": { "build": "tsc", "lint": "eslint .", "test": "vitest" } }
```

```json
// turbo.json - register tasks
{
  "tasks": {
    "build": { "dependsOn": ["^build"], "outputs": ["dist/**"] },
    "lint": {},
    "test": { "dependsOn": ["build"] }
  }
}
```

```json
// Root package.json - ONLY delegates, no task logic
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "turbo run build",
    "lint": "turbo run lint",
    "test": "turbo run test"
  }
}
```

```json
// DO NOT DO THIS - defeats parallelization
// Root package.json
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "cd apps/web && next build && cd ../api && tsc",
    "lint": "eslint apps/ packages/",
    "test": "vitest"
  }
}
```

Root Tasks (`//#taskname`) are ONLY for tasks that truly cannot exist in packages, such as Vitest Projects' `//#test`, repo-wide release scripts, or tooling that does not invoke `turbo` itself.

## Secondary Rule: `turbo run` vs `turbo`

**Always use `turbo run` when the command is written into code:**

```json
// package.json - ALWAYS "turbo run"
{
  "scripts": {
    "build": "turbo run build"
  }
}
```

```yaml
# CI workflows - ALWAYS "turbo run"
- run: turbo run build --affected
```

**The shorthand `turbo <tasks>` is ONLY for one-off terminal commands** typed directly by humans or agents. Never write `turbo build` into package.json, CI, or scripts.

## Quick Decision Trees

### "I need to configure a task"

```
Configure a task?
├─ Define task dependencies → references/configuration/tasks.md
├─ Lint/check-types (parallel + caching) → Use Transit Nodes pattern (see below)
├─ Specify build outputs → references/configuration/tasks.md#outputs
├─ Handle environment variables → references/environment/RULE.md
├─ Set up dev/watch tasks → references/configuration/tasks.md#persistent
├─ Package-specific config → references/configuration/RULE.md#package-configurations
└─ Global settings (cacheDir, daemon) → references/configuration/global-options.md
```

### "My cache isn't working"

```
Cache problems?
├─ Tasks run but outputs not restored → Missing `outputs` key
├─ Cache misses unexpectedly → references/caching/gotchas.md
├─ Need to debug hash inputs → Use --summarize or --dry
├─ Want to skip cache entirely → Use --force or cache: false
├─ Remote cache not working → references/caching/remote-cache.md
└─ Environment causing misses → references/environment/gotchas.md
```

### "I want to run only changed packages"

```
Run only what changed?
├─ Changed packages + dependents (RECOMMENDED) → turbo run build --affected
├─ Custom base branch → --affected --affected-base=origin/develop
├─ Manual git comparison → --filter=...[origin/main]
└─ See all filter options → references/filtering/RULE.md
```

**`--affected` is the primary way to run only changed packages.** It automatically compares against the default branch and includes dependents.

### "I want to filter packages"

```
Filter packages?
├─ Only changed packages → --affected (see above)
├─ By package name → --filter=web
├─ By directory → --filter=./apps/*
├─ Package + dependencies → --filter=web...
├─ Package + dependents → --filter=...web
└─ Complex combinations → references/filtering/patterns.md
```

### "Environment variables aren't working"

```
Environment issues?
├─ Vars not available at runtime → Strict mode filtering (default)
├─ Cache hits with wrong env → Var not in `env` key
├─ .env changes not causing rebuilds → .env not in `inputs`
├─ CI variables missing → references/environment/gotchas.md
└─ Framework vars (NEXT_PUBLIC_*) → Auto-included via inference
```

name: dg-roam-load-extension
description: Build, register, activate, and verify the local Discourse Graphs Roam extension, then run an optional feature test in the same Playwright context. Use for live apps/roam proof on Windows or macOS without repeating browser, login, and folder-loading setup.
---

# DG Roam Load Extension

Use this skill for one complete lifecycle: build `apps/roam`, open an authenticated slot, register `apps/roam/dist`, activate it, verify DG runtime readiness, run an optional caller test, capture proof, and close.

It composes with `dg-roam-playwright-session` for account/profile selection.

## Quick Start

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1
```

Use another slot for isolated work:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 2
```

The script builds by default, verifies `window.roamjs.extension.queryBuilder`, checks the DG settings UI, and writes proof under `local/roam-playwright/artifacts`.

To add feature-specific assertions without copying the loader, pass an ESM test module:

```sh
pnpm --filter roam playwright:load-extension -- --slot 1 --test-module ./local/roam-playwright/feature-proof.mjs
```

```js
export default {
  readySelector: "[data-testid='feature-ready']",
  async ready({ page }) {
    return page.evaluate(() => Boolean(window.myFeature?.ready));
  },
  async run({ page, outDir }) {
    await page.getByText("Expected output").waitFor();
    return { assertion: "passed" };
  },
  async cleanup({ page, state }) {
    // Remove only fixtures created by run().
  },
};
```

`run()` starts only after the standard DG runtime proof and any caller readiness hook succeeds. `cleanup()` runs when `run()` started, including after a failed assertion. Return JSON-serializable proof values.

## Options

- `--slot 1|2|3`: Select the Roam account/profile.
- `--skip-build`: Load the existing `apps/roam/dist` without rebuilding.
- `--headed`: Run with a visible Chromium window.
- `--keep-open`: Leave the browser open after loading.
- `--dist <path>`: Load a different Roam extension folder. Use only when intentionally testing another build output.
- `--registration-name <name>`: Developer Extensions row name. Defaults to the built folder name, usually `dist`.
- `--test-module <path>`: Caller readiness, test, and cleanup hooks. Absolute Windows paths and paths containing spaces are supported.
- `--out <path>` and `--screenshot-name <name>`: Proof artifact locations.
- `--timeout <ms>`: UI and readiness timeout. Defaults to `45000`.

## Folder Loading

Roam Depot's folder button calls `window.showDirectoryPicker()`, not an `<input type="file">`. The script installs a temporary in-page directory-picker shim backed by the files in `apps/roam/dist`.

The loader uses native Playwright clicks for developer mode and folder controls. It treats the extension row as registration only, then clicks the header or row refresh control when present and waits for DG runtime proof. Roam versions that activate automatically may expose no refresh control.

An IndexedDB clone warning for the fake directory handle is expected and classified separately. Other page exceptions fail the run. `last-run.json` includes phase timings and bounded browser diagnostics; failures also capture a dedicated screenshot and compact DOM state.

## Safety Notes

- Do not commit `.env`, browser profiles, or artifacts.
- Do not commit real Roam test account emails, graph names, graph URLs, or proof screenshots.
- Keep feature fixtures, command interactions, and assertions in the caller module. Do not add them to the generic loader.
- Do not change Supabase local/branch/production config as part of this skill.
- Do not run production-backend smoke tests in this workflow.
---

content.text:
# Evidence ledger and shared receipt rendering

Use the option A evidence ledger for verification. The same renderer supplies the parent journey and full-review gate ladder; their owning references define the phase keys. Render from observed records, never from the desired outcome.

## Record

Keep all existing fields in `verification.json`. Add `kind: "verification"`, structured `gates`, and `nextAction` for the display. Parent workflows save their own summary JSON and reference the same evidence without duplicating execution. The renderer reads:

| Field                                    | Meaning                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kind`                                   | `verification`, `workflow`, or `full-review`                                     |
| `title`                                  | Optional concise feature/result title                                            |
| `mode`                                   | `pre-pr` or `final` (default `final`)                                            |
| `sourceCheckout`, `sha`                  | Exact tested checkout and full target SHA                                        |
| `pr`                                     | `{number, url}` when a PR exists                                                 |
| `currentPrHead`, `clean`                 | Confirmed current PR head and clean feature checkout; required for final success |
| `dirtySourceFingerprint`, `bundleSha256` | Recorded build identity; keep other existing identity fields too                 |
| `gates`                                  | Verification array: `{name, status, detail?, sha?, url?, required?}`             |
| `phases`                                 | Workflow-specific phase objects: `{status, detail?, sha?, url?}`                 |
| `blockers`                               | Array of observed blocker descriptions, empty only when confirmed                |
| `nextAction`, `humanAcceptance`          | Concrete continuation and actual human decision, usually `Pending`               |

Gate statuses are `passed`, `failed`, `blocked`, `pending`, `partial`, `unknown`, `waived`, or `not-applicable`. Missing phase statuses stay unknown. Waived/not-applicable gates need a recorded reason in `detail`; a display cannot grant a waiver. A gate is required unless explicitly marked `required: false`, which is reserved for clearly identified supplemental or unrelated baseline checks with their disposition in `detail`.

List every required check for this change. Group commands when that improves readability, but keep acceptance behavior distinct from build/test results. For final Roam UI work, include screenshot and walkthrough inspection as separate required gates unless explicitly waived. Frame sampling or decode success alone leaves required complete-video inspection partial. Keep artifact paths and per-artifact inspection in the original receipt. Unknown diagnostics or a stale evidence SHA must remain visible.

Example shape (illustrative values, not a run result):

```json
{
  "kind": "verification",
  "mode": "final",
  "sourceCheckout": "/feature/checkout",
  "sha": "full-tested-sha",
  "pr": { "number": 42, "url": "https://github.com/example/extension/pull/42" },
  "currentPrHead": "full-tested-sha",
  "clean": true,
  "gates": [
    {
      "name": "Required commands",
      "status": "passed",
      "detail": "Actual command results"
    },
    {
      "name": "Acceptance behavior",
      "status": "passed",
      "detail": "Observed fixture assertions"
    },
    {
      "name": "Screenshot inspection",
      "status": "passed",
      "detail": "Every final screenshot inspected"
    },
    {
      "name": "Walkthrough inspection",
      "status": "partial",
      "detail": "Complete relevant playback pending"
    }
  ],
  "blockers": [],
  "nextAction": "Inspect the complete relevant walkthrough.",
  "humanAcceptance": "Pending"
}
```

The renderer derives `Verified`/`Complete` only from completed required gates and matching final identity. It does not consume an optimistic free-text `status` as a verdict. A partial, missing, or mismatched gate remains incomplete. The caller still owns the actual required-check list and evidence assessment.

## Render and deliver

```sh
node /path/to/mg-verify-project-change/scripts/render-receipt.mjs verification.json output-directory
```

This writes `receipt.html`, `receipt.fragment.html`, and `receipt.md` from one record, with supporting identity details collapsed. Resolve the script from the canonical skill directory; it works from another working directory and through managed links.

Show one handoff receipt in the host's supported format. In T3 Code, pass the full saved HTML to `html_preview`, then `html_render`. In Codex, use the available documented inline HTML/visualization surface; if unavailable, give compact Markdown and a direct link to the saved HTML. Claude Code Desktop and CLI hosts use the Markdown fallback and HTML link. Do not install or switch hosts solely for a receipt. A calling parent may consolidate these gates into its receipt instead of displaying all child cards again.

Keep required [media delivery](media-handoff.md) alongside the receipt, including saved evidence for partial and blocked runs. The receipt does not imply human acceptance, merge approval, or publication.

- Offline Roam graphs skip DG enrollment, sync, sharing, import, and cloud canvas connections. {"title":"Keep offline Roam graphs out of DG cloud services","description":"## Problem

* DG uses the Roam graph name to identify the space. Hosted and offline graphs can have the same name, so DG can confuse two separate graphs during sync, sharing, and cloud canvas use.
* Fix the boundary before extending web publishing to Roam. The source review confirmed the collision in code. Production exposure is unverified.

## Solution

* Keep offline graphs local-only. Use Roam’s `roamAlphaAPI.graph.type` to disable DG cloud features before any space enrollment, sync, sharing/import, cloud canvas, or web publishing. Explain why in the UI.
* Require the server to verify the hosted graph binding and the caller’s permissions. Do not treat the graph name, client-reported type, or canvas room ID as authorization.

## Done When

* Same-name offline and hosted graphs stay separate. Offline or unverified graphs cannot connect to a hosted DG space or cloud canvas, and denied enrollment leaves existing space data unchanged.
* Offline graphs still support local features and local canvases. Authorized hosted graphs can use cloud features and reconnect after a temporary network outage.
* Automated checks cover same-name graphs, graph switching, and server-side rejection independent of the UI.

## Out of Scope

* Offline cloud support, cross-client space IDs, and replacing RIDs with node UUIDs. See [FEE-953](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-953/should-dg-support-cloud-features-for-offline-roam-graphs>).
* Obsidian vault identity. See [ENG-2086](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/ENG-2086/the-same-db-id-is-used-across-vaults-which-breaks-sync>) and [FEE-889](<https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/issue/FEE-889/sync-nodes-between-personal-local-vaults>).

## Notes

* [Roam graph type API](<https://roamdocs.fyi/developer-documentation/roam-alpha-api>) · [DG space URI helper](<https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/blob/9faef8689dcea7070103e0c16470fb294735d342/apps/roam/src/utils/canonicalRoamUrl.ts>)

name: dg-engineering-writing-style
description: Draft and revise engineering emails, chat messages, requests, follow-ups, status updates, engineering tickets, PR comments, issue reports, release notes, technical documentation, and other team writing in the shared Discourse Graphs style. # DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

The revised ticket just uses the graph type Roam reports to decide whether the plugin should start cloud features.

A **DG space** is the database record DG uses to group a graph’s cloud data. For Roam, the plugin looks up that record using a URL derived from the graph name. By “linked,” I meant independently verifying that the request came from the hosted Roam graph associated with that record. The revised ticket just uses the graph type Roam reports to decide whether the plugin should start cloud features.

**Client-side is enough for the duplicate-name bug.** The plugin knows whether the open graph is offline. It can check that before using the graph name to enroll in a DG space, sync, share or import nodes, or connect to a cloud canvas. Put the check where each operation starts so background sync and saved settings respect it too. A hosted graph that temporarily loses connectivity still counts as hosted.

Two limits worth knowing:

- Older plugin versions can still hit the bug until users update. The server will continue accepting requests through the existing paths.
- If an offline copy has a canvas whose latest edits exist only in the cloud, it can show only the snapshot saved locally. That could be an older version or an empty canvas.

**The automated checks** use fake graphs and mock cloud calls. They check that a same-name offline graph skips enrollment and can’t reuse a cached hosted session, that switching graphs during enrollment stops the next step, that saved cloud canvas settings select local mode, and that hosted enrollment retries after simulated connectivity loss. They don’t exercise a real canvas in Roam.

I’d keep the small same-name regression test because it catches the exact bug. The ticket can describe the expected behavior without making automated checks a separate acceptance criterion. The current local draft also gates feedback and diagnostics and includes server-side enrollment hardening. Those are beyond the duplicate-name fix you described.
